newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan court acquits ex-spymaster of treason.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan court acquits ex-spymaster of treason.

text.p: A Pakistani court on Tuesday acquitted a former spymaster, Imtiaz Ahmed, of committing treason in 1989 by allegedly conspiring to topple then-prime minister Benazir Bhutto, the official APP news agency said.
It said special judge Abdul Hamid Khattak also acquitted four other men, including former commerce minister Malik Mohammad Naeem, accused in the so-called "Operation Midnight Jackals" case.
Imtiaz, a retired army brigadier, was the chief of the Intelligence Bureau in the first government of Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif from 1990 to 1993.
He and a co-accused, retired major Mohammad Aamer, were charged with high treason, which under Pakistani law can be punishable by the death penalty.

A police report on their arrest in 1994 had said that both acted at the behest of Bhutto's political opponents in trying to subvert the loyalties of ruling party deputies in September and October of 1989, when the two served in the powerful Inter-Services Intelligence Agency.
Bhutto had blamed intelligence agencies when then president Ghulam Ishaq Khan sacked her 20-month-old government in 1990 with apparent army backing.
Bhutto was returned to power in late 1993 but was sacked by President Farooq Leghari last November on disputed charges of misrule.
